newsitem.title: CHINA: Herzog says human rights, trade key China issues.
newsitem.headline: Herzog says human rights, trade key China issues.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog said on Wednesday both human rights and trade were important issues in Sino-German relations and that one did not have to be sacrificed for the other.

Herzog told reporters at a news briefing in Beijing that he had raised human rights issues and the importance of Sino-German economic exchanges in his talks with Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng.
"Both matters are important but I don't think that one has to be chosen over the other," Herzog said.
German business leaders based in China had expressed confidence in the country's market-oriented reforms, Herzog said, adding that he hoped more Germans would invest in China.
"We have to catch up here," he said. "In the next century China is going to play an enormous part as a world power."
Herzog is scheduled to fly to China's industrial and commercial hub of Shanghai on Thursday.

Sino-German ties have been strained in recent months by disputes over Tibet. Herzog has been under pressure at home to stress human rights in ties with Beijing after a recent crackdown on dissent by China's communist rulers.
A Beijing court last week rejected the appeal of dissident and former student leader Wang Dan and upheld his 11-year jail term for plotting to subvert the government.
